`case_study:super-micro-2023-2026` · tickers US-SMCI · confidence: verified

Split-adjusted (10:1, Oct 2024): ~$4-7 in 2022-early 2023 -> intraday ~$122.9 (Mar 2024), joining the S&P 500: ~17-30x [prices from memory, unverified]. Revenue roughly doubled FY23->FY24 (~$7bn -> ~$15bn) on Nvidia GPU server racks and liquid cooling. Then: gross margin fell to 11.3% (June 2024 qtr) from 17%; Hindenburg short report (Aug 27 2024: accounting red flags, related parties, export-control issues); 10-K delayed; Ernst & Young resigned Oct 30 2024 saying it could no longer rely on management/audit-committee representations (-33% day). Low ~$17 (Nov 2024), ~-86% from peak [unverified exact]. BDO hired Nov 2024; overdue reports filed Feb 2025 without restatement, but BDO issued adverse opinions on internal controls. Margins kept sliding (9.3% FQ1'26; 6.4% adj FQ2'26). March 2026: US indicted co-founder Wally Liaw and two others for diverting ~$2.5bn of Nvidia-based servers (~$510m reaching China); stock -33% in a day; company not charged. EARLY RED FLAGS visible before the peak: 2018 Nasdaq delisting for late filings, 2020 SEC accounting settlement (~$17.5m) [unverified], rehiring of executives tied to that episode, related-party suppliers, and falling gross margin while revenue soared (a commoditised assembler). Who caught it: momentum buyers on the way up; Hindenburg on the way down. LESSON: revenue hypergrowth in a low-moat assembler plus a known governance history is a peak-hype setup; margin compression is the first tell.

- **Start → end:** ~$4-7 split-adj (2022-23) [unverified] → peak ~$122.9 (Mar 2024); ~$17 low (Nov 2024); ~$20-60 range 2025-26 (~17-30x up, then -86%)
- **EPS vs rerating:** EPS + rerating up; margin collapse down
- **Max drawdown:** ~-86% (Mar-Nov 2024)
- **Early signal:** up: AI rack share; down: prior SEC case, 2018 delisting, GM 17%->11%
- **Who caught it:** Hindenburg Research (short)
- **Ended/stalled:** Aug-Nov 2024 blow-up; Mar 2026 indictment
- **Lesson:** governance history + commodity margins = fragile multibagger
- **Sources:** [1](https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/super-micro-computers-shares-plunge-after-accounting-firm-115309047) · [2](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/super-micro-shares-drop-ernst-young-resigns-amid-accounting-concerns) · [3](https://www.fool.com/investing/2024/11/04/what-is-happening-at-super-micro-computer-heres-wh) · [4](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/super-micro-just-reported-lowest-192300795.html) · [5](https://www.ibtimes.com/supermicro-stock-crashes-33-after-co-founder-arrested-25-billion-nvidia-chip-smuggling-scheme-3799850) · [6](https://www.cfodive.com/news/supermicro-cofounder-charged-smuggling-servers-china/815346/)

`theme:sector-fmcg-consumer` · confidence: single-source · tickers: HINDUNILVR, NESTLEIND, BRITANNIA, ITC, DABUR, MARICO, COLPAL, TATACONSUM, GODREJCP

**How it makes money:** Brand + distribution moat; pricing power over commodities; negative working capital, very high RoCE.

**Metrics that matter:**
- Underlying volume growth
- Price/mix contribution
- Gross margin
- EBITDA margin
- A&P % of sales
- Rural vs urban growth
- Direct reach / distribution
- Market share (NielsenIQ)

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Agri/commodity inputs -> manufacturing (often outsourced) -> brand & marketing -> distributors/super-stockists -> kirana (~70–80%), modern trade, e-com/quick commerce. The brand owner captures most of the margin; distributors and kiranas hold thin margins; quick commerce shifts bargaining power.

**Cycle drivers:** Rural income & monsoon, food inflation, commodity prices, GST/tax, competitive intensity (D2C, regional), channel shifts.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- NielsenIQ FMCG quarterly snapshot (volume, rural/urban)
- IMD monsoon & reservoir levels
- Labour Bureau rural wages
- CPI food inflation (MoSPI)
- Tractor/2W sales as rural proxy
- GST collections (monthly)

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: volume-led growth, category creation, premiumisation, cost leadership, early digital/quick-commerce adoption. Losers: price-led growth, share loss to D2C and regional brands, diversification bets.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/E 40–60x leaders (peak 2019–21, 55–75x for HUL/Nestle), compressing to ~45–55x by 2024–26. FMCG index ~33.8x vs 41.8x 7-yr median (Jun 2026). Troughs: 2008 (relative), 2013.

**Current state (Nov 2026):** Q2 FY27 FMCG value growth 8.6% (six-quarter high; Q1 6.8%), rural 10.6% vs urban 5.8%. HUL Q2 FY27 USG ~15% and UVG ~7% per one source (verify; looks high), with management citing a step-up in rural markets.

**Classic traps:**
- Paying peak multiples for slowing volume
- Pricing-led growth reverses with deflation
- Quick-commerce margin dilution
- Mistaking defensive for cheap

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:BSE:q3fy27-revenue-record-above-1566cr`
- **Method:** sector cycle/lead indicator · **P(ours)** 0.60 · **P(base)** 0.45 · resolve by 2027-02-28
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): H1 operational revenue ₹2,999 cr (+48%); transaction charges ₹2,456 cr (+60%). Index-options premium ADTV: Q1 FY27 ₹29,615 cr, Q2 ₹22,531 cr ('first sequential quarterly contraction'), then 'a decisive recovery in September and a record-breaking October 2026… highest ever monthly index options premium ADTV of Rs. 35,481' crore; record single-day expiry premium ₹85,356 cr on 22-Oct-2026. MSCI derivatives collaboration. Screener revenue (₹ cr): Q4 FY26 1,564, Q1 FY27 1,566, Q2 FY27 1,433; OPM 67–68%.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Lead indicator: premium ADTV drives ~80% of revenue. A linear fit of Q1/Q2 (revenue ≈ ₹1,009 cr + 0.0188 × ADTV) says a Q3 average ADTV above ~₹29.7k cr beats the record; October alone ran at ₹35.5k. Risk: November–December fade or a SEBI F&O tightening. Above base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** A naive forecaster gives a fast-growing exchange setting a new quarterly revenue record after a down quarter roughly 45% (records are set in about half of quarters in an uptrend).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if BSE's consolidated revenue from operations for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 (results filing; screener.in 'Sales') is > ₹1,566 cr.
- **Resolution source:** BSE Ltd Q3 FY27 results (NSE) / screener.in consolidated quarterly table
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/BSE1_11112026122425_NSeintimation11112026.pdf; https://www.screener.in/company/BSE/consolidated/
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified

body:
Uttam Sugar: the UP cane price alone ≈ the sugar realisation; each ₹10/qtl moves EBITDA 15–19%. The Oct-2026 OMC ethanol tender
excludes cane-juice/B-heavy ethanol (the company's distillery feedstock) — absent from its Oct-31 results deck. **Rules:** for any
business with administered prices, keep a dated table (last value, next decision date, whether the company's filings mention it).
Seasonal balance sheets need average capital (net debt ₹30 cr Sep vs ₹712 cr Mar). When core EPS = reported, valuation temperature
(15.2x vs own 10-yr median 8.0x) can be the binding read. Card can't express *partial* loss of a government input (core-asset trigger
is yes/no). Cyclical upside tail (model 0.8% ≥3x vs a stock that did 12.7x in 2020–23) is likely too thin → covered by pre-registered fix (3).
Frame hygiene: industry_map's FMCG includes agri-commodity processors. 8/8 live cards size 0; 3/3 recent draws ROIC < CoE.
